question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ -2 & 0 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $Σ$ shown above. Given that $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ which of the following could be the matrix $V?$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if  $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of a $3\times 2$ matrix $A,$ then

- $Σ$ is a $3\times 2$ matrix with nonnegative elements on the main diagonal and zeroes outside the main diagonal,

- $U$ is an orthogonal $3\times 3$ matrix,

- $V$ is an orthogonal $2\times 2$ matrix.

Let's find the singular value decomposition of $A$ using the usual algorithm.

- **Step 1.** Compute ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ -2 & 0 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ -2 & 0 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ -2 & 0 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8 & 2 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step 2.** Find the singular values: From the matrix $Σ,$ we deduce that ${\sigma }_{1}=3$ and ${\sigma }_{2}=2.$

- **Step 3.** Find the right singular vectors of $A$ (i.e., the unit eigenvectors of ${A}^{T}\,A$):

- For ${\lambda }_{1}={\sigma }_{1}^{2}=9,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A-9I & =[\begin{aligned}8 & 2 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}]-9[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 2 & -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $({A}^{T}\,A-9I)v=0$ gives the unit eigenvector

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}].
$$

- For ${\lambda }_{2}={\sigma }_{2}^{2}=4,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A-4I & =[\begin{aligned}8 & 2 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}]-4[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $({A}^{T}\,A-4I)v=0$ gives the unit eigenvector

$$
{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, we construct the matrix $V:$

$$
V=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]
$$
